correctness.rationale: For each c, log-curvature equality gives Z_T/Z_S = exp(AR+B); multiplication by exp(cR²) and continuation of the Gaussian-damped bilateral Laplace transforms give a shift by k=A/(2c). Fourier uniqueness of the finite measures yields the pointwise gauge by continuity. If the two shifts coincide, c1≠c2 forces zero shift. Otherwise taking logarithms produces a global affine first difference with quadratic coefficient α=(c1 k1−c2 k2)/(k1−k2). Subtracting the quadratic-affine solution gives a bounded periodic logarithm. Growth rules out α>0, and α=0 forces b=0 by growth of S and then k1=k2=0 by growth of T. With α=−a<0, the compatibility equation gives the stated shifts, and periodicity and the common envelope slope give sufficiency. The alias-to-spectrum ratio has nonzero exponential slope times a bounded, bounded-away-from-zero factor, so it cannot be constant. The Fourier window squared gives c=2π/σ²; the unit-window intensity formula transforms with area Jacobian one and frequency second-derivative factor σ², giving 1/(2c).
